sentences.text: Laricola was a genus of extinct birds resembling gulls that lived in Europe during the late Oligocene and early Miocene.
This bird possessed proportionally longer and more slender legs than living species of the family Laromorphae.
The genus Laricola was described by Mlíkovský in 2002.
Milne-Edwards previously classified three species of Laricola as belonging to the genus Larus between 1863 and 1868.
The type species of the genus Laricola is Laricola elegans, described by Milne-Edwards in 1868.
Fossils of Laricola have been found in France and are also alleged to come from the Czech Republic.
The genus Laricola contains five distinct species.
Laricola intermedia is a species within the genus, described by De Pietri et al. in 2014.
Laricola robusta is a species within the genus, described by De Pietri et al. in 2014.
Laricola belongs to the parent group Laromorphae.
Laricola lived between the Rupelian and Aquitanian stages, from 33.9 to 20.45 million years ago.
